taglines.genesis: The book of beginnings: God makes a good world, humanity breaks it, and God promises to bless every nation through one family.
taglines.exodus: The book of Israel's rescue from slavery in Egypt, the covenant God makes with them at Mount Sinai, and the tent where he comes to live among them.
taglines.leviticus: How a holy God can live among an unholy people: sacrifice, priesthood, purity, and a whole life set apart for him and for the neighbor.
taglines.numbers: The book of the wilderness: a people counted and ordered around God's presence refuses to trust him, dies in the desert, and leaves its children at the edge of the promised land.
taglines.deuteronomy: Moses' farewell sermons on the plains of Moab: the covenant restated for a new generation, calling Israel to love the one God with the whole heart before it enters the land.
taglines.joshua: The book of the promised land: Israel crosses the Jordan under Joshua, takes hold of Canaan, divides it among the tribes, and renews the covenant with God.
taglines.judges: The dark years between Joshua and the kings, when Israel kept forgetting God and God kept raising up flawed deliverers to rescue them.
taglines.ruth: A short, carefully told story of famine, loss, and loyal love, in which a Moabite widow becomes the great-grandmother of King David.
taglines.1-samuel: The story of how Israel moved from judges to kings, told through three lives: Samuel the prophet, Saul the first king, and David the shepherd God chose to replace him.
taglines.2-samuel: The story of David's reign over Israel: how the shepherd became king, how God promised him a house that would last forever, and how his own sin tore that house apart.
taglines.1-kings: The story of Israel's kings from Solomon's glory and temple to a kingdom split in two, judged by one question: did the king walk with the LORD?
taglines.2-kings: The story of Israel and Judah from Elijah's departure to the fall of Samaria and of Jerusalem, told as the long working out of God's word through prophets and kings.
taglines.1-chronicles: Israel's story retold from Adam to David for a small, returned people, asking whether God's promises to David and his temple still stand.
taglines.2-chronicles: The second half of the Chronicler's history: Solomon's temple, the kings of Judah, the fall of Jerusalem, and a closing word of return.
taglines.ezra: The story of the first exiles to come home from Babylon, the rebuilding of God's temple under Persian rule, and a scribe who called a small, battered people back to the law of Moses.
taglines.nehemiah: A Persian court official's own account of rebuilding Jerusalem's walls, renewing the covenant under the law of Moses, and fighting to keep a restored people faithful.
taglines.esther: A tale of exile, court intrigue, and reversal in which a Jewish queen and her cousin save their people from annihilation in the Persian Empire, and God is never named.
taglines.job: A great poem about an innocent man who loses everything, argues with his friends and with God, and meets God in the storm.
taglines.psalms: Israel's book of prayer and song: 150 poems of praise, lament, thanks, and wisdom, gathered into five books and prayed by God's people for three thousand years.
taglines.proverbs: Israel's book of practical wisdom: a father's instruction and hundreds of short sayings on living well in God's world, all rooted in the fear of the LORD.
taglines.ecclesiastes: A wise man's honest search for what lasts in a world where everything passes like a breath, framed by a teacher who points the reader back to the fear of God.
taglines.song-of-solomon: A sequence of love poems between a woman and a man, celebrating desire, delight, and faithful love, which Jews and Christians have also long read as a song of God's love for his people.
taglines.isaiah: The great prophet of God's holiness, judgment, and comfort, whose vision runs from the sins of Jerusalem to a new heavens and a new earth.
taglines.jeremiah: The prophet who watched Jerusalem fall, pleading with a people who would not listen and promising a new covenant written on the heart.
taglines.lamentations: Five poems of grief over the fall of Jerusalem in 587 or 586 BC, prayers that refuse to look away from ruin and still address God.
taglines.ezekiel: The visions, sign-acts, and oracles of a priest exiled to Babylon, who saw God's glory leave Jerusalem's temple and saw it return.
taglines.daniel: Stories of faithful exiles in a pagan court and visions of beastly empires, both declaring that the Most High rules and that God's kingdom will outlast them all.
taglines.hosea: A prophet told to marry an unfaithful wife becomes the living picture of God's wounded, relentless covenant love for a people who have gone after other gods.
